Boston Dynamics outlines an hour-long Atlas build ambition

A prototype-shop video describes roughly one-day builds today and closer links between machining, assembly and engineering.

Humanoids Daily ↗14 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

Inside prototype operations

A new Boston Dynamics film shows Atlas teams combining construction, testing, maintenance and repair. Senior technical programme manager Katie Conner describes roughly one-day robot builds today and an ambition for approximately an hour next year.

Machining close to engineering

Keeping precision work such as gear cutting in-house lets engineers discuss changes directly with machinists. Staff describe some parts reaching assembly the same or next day, alongside process development and robotic arms used in assembly.

Build time is not shipment throughput

The hour is a target, not an achieved result, and the film does not establish a shipment rate. Faster prototype work can accelerate hardware iteration, but its process boundaries must be understood before comparisons with other production lines.
